name: Overhead Single-Arm Kettlebell Waiter Carry
description: The single-arm overhead kettlebell waiter carry challenges the entire lateral and anti-rotation core stabilization system by requiring the athlete to walk while holding a kettlebell locked out overhead in one hand. The overhead unilateral load creates a large lateral flexion and rotational demand on the contralateral core musculature, the shoulder girdle stabilizers, and the thoracic spine extensors simultaneously. It is both a core stability and shoulder integrity exercise that is highly transferable to functional strength tasks.

execution.starting_position: Clean and press a kettlebell to full lockout overhead in one hand. Stand tall with the arm straight, elbow locked, bicep beside the ear.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with a light-to-moderate weight to establish shoulder stability and walking pattern before increasing load.
steps: Step 1: Lock the kettlebell out overhead with the working arm straight and elbow fully extended.
Step 2: Pack the shoulder by depressing the scapula and externally rotating the arm.
Step 3: Walk at a controlled pace for the prescribed distance or time.
Step 4: Keep the torso upright — resist any lateral flexion toward the weighted side.
Step 5: At the end of the distance, carefully lower the kettlebell and switch hands.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe normally throughout. Maintain a constant bracing level.
common_mistakes: Allowing the elbow to bend — the arm must remain fully locked out
Laterally flexing the trunk toward the weighted side — the spine should remain perfectly vertical
safety_considerations: Ensure full shoulder external rotation and scapular depression before beginning — a loose overhead position is a safety risk
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Walk with full arm extension maintained. Distance typically 20–40 metres per set.
coaching_cues: Bicep beside the ear — arm is a pillar
